title: SIGMo: High-Throughput Batched Subgraph Isomorphism on GPUs for Molecular Matching
problem: Subgraph isomorphism is NP-complete and computationally expensive; state-of-the-art frameworks insufficient for large-scale molecular matching
motivation: Drug discovery requires fast molecular matching via subgraph isomorphism; batch processing enables high throughput
method: The framework uses SYCL (a programming language for GPUs) to write code that runs on AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA hardware. It narrows down candidate matches through multiple filtering stages using neighborhood signatures—fingerprints encoding the local graph structure around each node—which eliminates most non-matches before expensive computation. Once filtered, it runs a depth-first search on the GPU to find actual matching subgraphs, using parallel processing to explore candidate paths efficiently.
key_novelty: It combines multi-level signature-based filtering with GPU-accelerated depth-first search for subgraph matching, all in portable SYCL that works on AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPUs.
limitations: Specific to molecular matching domain constraints; generalization unclear
